question: What is the term for : "A literary or rhetorical device in which the opposite of what is expected occurs"?
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Situational Irony**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • **Situational Irony** refers to a literary or rhetorical device in which the opposite of what is expected occurs. (स्थितिजन्य विडंबना) • **Example:** A fire station burns down. This is ironic because the place dedicated to preventing fires becomes the victim of one. • Situational Irony is used to create a twist or surprise in a narrative where the outcome is contrary to expectations. (अपेक्षाओं के विपरीत परिणाम उत्पन्न करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है।) Therefore, the correct answer is: **Situational Irony**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Antithesis** (विरोधाभास): A rhetorical device in which two opposite ideas are contrasted in the same sentence. • **Example:** "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times" is an example of antithesis. • **Verbal Irony** (शाब्दिक विडंबना): A rhetorical device where the speaker says something but means the opposite. • **Example:** Saying "What a lovely day!" during a thunderstorm is verbal irony. • **Paradox** (विरोधाभास): A statement that contradicts itself but still might be true. • **Example:** "Less is more" is a paradox because it contradicts itself yet conveys a deeper truth. 3e:Tba6, The correct answer is: **4) Kantianism**.
